name: get_project
description: The overview of the whole project: CPU, blocks (OB/FC/FB with their networks), data blocks with variables, PLC data types, tags, and whether it compiles. Call this first when you start working on a request.

name: get_block
description: One block in full: its interface (Input, Output, InOut, Static, Temp, Return) and every network with its language and code (SCL / STL text, LAD as a cell grid). Call this before you change a block.

block.description: OB1, FC2, FB1 or the block name

name: write_network
description: Writes one network of a block: replaces network n (1-based) or appends a new one when network is 0 or missing. SCL / STL: the whole code in code. LAD: the cells (see the system prompt). Returns the compile messages of the block: fix every error.

code.description: SCL or STL code, lines separated by \n

name: delete_network
description: Deletes network n (1-based) of a block.

name: create_block
description: Creates an FC or an FB (without networks: write them with write_network). For an FB, instance_db creates its instance DB too.

instance_db.description: FB only: the name of a new instance DB

name: set_interface
description: Replaces the whole interface of an FC / FB / OB (an OB has only Temp, an FC no Static, an FB no Return).

name: add_db_variables
description: Adds variables to a global data block (a variable that exists already gets the new type / start value). Creates the DB when it does not exist.

number.description: for a new DB: optional, the next free number

name: add_tags
description: Adds PLC tags (symbols) to the tag table; a tag that exists already gets the new type / address.

name: compile
description: Compiles the whole project and returns every error and warning (block, network, line). Call it after your changes and before you finish.

name: read_values
description: Reads live values from the simulated CPU (it must be in RUN with the current program downloaded): absolute addresses, "Tags", "DB".Var. Use it to debug: what the inputs, outputs and variables really are. wait_ms waits first (up to 10000), e.g. for a timer to run out after set_inputs.

name: set_inputs
description: Operates the simulated inputs, like the user on the I/O screen: digital inputs (bits of I, e.g. %I0.5 or "Start_PB") true / false, analog inputs (IW words of the analog channels) 0..27648. Use it to test the program: press a button, read_values, release it. A push button pressed stays pressed until you set it false again.

name: get_diagnostics
description: The CPU mode, why it stopped, and the last entries of the diagnostic buffer (programming errors such as an array index out of range, a cycle time overrun).

name: download_and_run
description: Compiles, downloads the program to the simulated CPU and switches it to RUN. The user is asked first and may say no. Use it when you need live values of new code.
